claims.quote: You ask me how we regulate wages; I can only reply that there is no idea in the modern social economy which at all corresponds with what was meant by wages in your day.
claims.description: An economy in which wages and money have been abolished.

claims.quote: But the credit given the worker at the government storehouse answers to his wages with us.
claims.description: Workers receive an annual credit at government stores in place of money wages.

claims.quote: His title," replied Dr. Leete, "is his humanity. The basis of his claim is the fact that he is a man.
claims.description: Every citizen receives an equal share of the national product simply by being human, like a universal equal income.

claims.quote: We leave no possible ground for any complaint of injustice," replied Dr. Leete, "by requiring precisely the same measure of service from all.
claims.description: All workers are required to give the same effort, their best, rather than the same output.

claims.quote: So you see that though we have abolished poverty and the fear of it, and inordinate luxury with the hope of it, we have not touched the greater part of the motives which underlay the love of money in former times, or any of those which prompted the supremer sorts of effort.
claims.description: Poverty and extreme luxury are abolished.

claims.quote: Now that industry of whatever sort is no longer self-service, but service of the nation, patriotism, passion for humanity, impel the worker as in your day they did the soldier.
claims.description: All industry is national service, and workers are moved by patriotism instead of profit.

claims.quote: The army of industry is an army, not alone by virtue of its perfect organization, but by reason also of the ardor of self-devotion which animates its members.
claims.description: The labor force is organized as a national industrial army.

claims.quote: With us, diligence in the national service is the sole and certain way to public repute, social distinction, and official power.
claims.description: Honor, rank and office awarded according to diligence in national service rather than wealth.

claims.quote: As we entered, Edith said that there was one of these great distributing establishments in each ward of the city, so that no residence was more than five or ten minutes' walk from one of them.
claims.description: Public distribution stores placed in every ward so every home is within a few minutes' walk of one.

claims.quote: There was no display of goods in the great windows, or any device to advertise wares, or attract custom.
claims.description: Advertising and window display disappear from retail.

claims.quote: The goods are the nation's.
claims.description: All goods for sale are owned by the nation, and clerks have no motive to push sales.

claims.quote: These printed cards, for which the government authorities are responsible, give us all the information we can possibly need.
claims.description: Government-certified product information labels giving make, materials, qualities and price.

claims.quote: He took down her order on a tablet with a pencil which made two copies, of which he gave one to her, and enclosing the counterpart in a small receptacle, dropped it into a transmitting tube.
claims.description: Orders written in duplicate and sent instantly by pneumatic tube to a central warehouse.

claims.quote: The duplicate of the order," said Edith as she turned away from the counter, after the clerk had punched the value of her purchase out of the credit card she gave him,
claims.description: Purchases paid with a personal credit card from which the value is deducted at the counter.

claims.quote: The assortment in all is exactly the same, representing as it does in each case samples of all the varieties produced or imported by the United States.
claims.description: Every store nationwide offers samples of the complete range of goods produced or imported by the country.

claims.quote: The goods, with these exceptions, are all at the great central warehouse of the city, to which they are shipped directly from the producers.
claims.description: Retail by sample showrooms, with goods stocked at a central city warehouse shipped straight from producers.

claims.quote: You avoid one handling of the goods, and eliminate the retailer altogether, with his big profit and the army of clerks it goes to support.
claims.description: Direct distribution eliminates retailers and most retail clerks, saving labor and cost.

claims.quote: Bales of cloth are placed on spindles and turned by machinery, and the cutter, who also has a machine, works right through one bale after another till exhausted, when another man takes his place;
claims.description: Mechanized order-filling in the central warehouse, with machine cutting of goods.

claims.quote: The packages are then delivered by larger tubes to the city districts, and thence distributed to the houses.
claims.description: Citywide pneumatic tube network delivering purchased goods to homes.

claims.quote: You may understand how quickly it is all done when I tell you that my order will probably be at home sooner than I could have carried it from here.
claims.description: Home delivery of purchases faster than the shopper could carry them home.

claims.quote: The system is the same," Edith explained; "the village sample shops are connected by transmitters with the central county warehouse, which may be twenty miles away.
claims.description: Rural shops linked to county warehouses twenty miles away by the same tube delivery system.

claims.quote: The rents which the nation receives for these houses vary, according to size, elegance, and location, so that everybody can find something to suit.
claims.description: The nation owns all housing and rents it at varying prices to citizens with equal incomes.

claims.quote: Well, you see, it could not be so nowadays; for everybody's income is known, and it is known that what is spent one way must be saved another.
claims.description: Because all incomes are equal and public, ostentatious spending to appear rich disappears.

claims.quote: All the really fine singers and players are in the musical service, and the rest of us hold our peace for the main part.
claims.description: Professional musicians organized as a public musical service, so amateurs rarely perform.

claims.quote: The card bore the date "September 12, 2000," and contained the longest programme of music I had ever seen.
claims.description: Published daily programme schedules for continuous music service.

claims.quote: She made me sit down comfortably, and, crossing the room, so far as I could see, merely touched one or two screws, and at once the room was filled with the music of a grand organ anthem;
claims.description: Live music played into the home at the touch of a control, with volume adjusted to the room.

claims.quote: These halls are connected by telephone with all the houses of the city whose people care to pay the small fee, and there are none, you may be sure, who do not.
claims.description: Subscription music broadcasting by telephone wire from concert halls to every home in the city.

claims.quote: The corps of musicians attached to each hall is so large that, although no individual performer, or group of performers, has more than a brief part, each day's programme lasts through the twenty-four hours.
claims.description: Round-the-clock 24-hour music programming.

claims.quote: There are on that card for to-day, as you will see if you observe closely, distinct programmes of four of these concerts, each of a different order of music from the others, being now simultaneously performed, and any one of the four pieces now going on that you prefer, you can hear by merely pressing the button
claims.description: Several simultaneous music channels the listener chooses between with a button.

claims.quote: All our bedchambers have a telephone attachment at the head of the bed by which any person who may be sleepless can command music at pleasure, of the sort suited to the mood.
claims.description: Bedside receivers that let anyone listen to music on demand at any hour.

claims.quote: We require, indeed, by law that every man shall serve the nation for a fixed period, instead of leaving him his choice, as you did, between working, stealing, or starving.
claims.description: Compulsory universal labor service to the nation for a fixed term of years.

claims.quote: In fact, you will find, Mr. West, as you come to know us, that there is far less interference of any sort with personal liberty nowadays than you were accustomed to.
claims.description: Less state interference with personal liberty than in the nineteenth century, outside the labor-service law.

claims.quote: The fact that the nation is the sole capitalist and land-owner of course restricts the individual's possessions to his annual credit, and what personal and household belongings he may have procured with it.
claims.description: The nation is the only owner of capital and land.

claims.quote: His credit, like an annuity in your day, ceases on his death, with the allowance of a fixed sum for funeral expenses.
claims.description: Personal credit ends at death apart from a fixed funeral allowance, so money cannot be inherited.

claims.quote: The articles, not being salable, would be of no value to him except for their actual use or the enjoyment of their beauty.
claims.description: Because goods cannot be sold, accumulating possessions becomes a burden rather than wealth.

claims.quote: The nation takes charge of the resigned chattels, and turns such as are of value into the common stock once more.
claims.description: Unwanted inherited belongings returned to the nation's common stock.
